findings.finding: The proof writes the empty set as each argument of I_n, although the referenced definition uses the dedicated empty-sequence symbol.
findings.controlling_evidence: I_n relates equal-length finite sequences and the preceding definition writes I_n(emptyseq,emptyseq); the set-theoretic empty set is not the stipulated sequence notation.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use emptyseq in both occurrences and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-022 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proof takes ordinary set unions of element and finite-sequence domains, and then of the M and N sides, without ensuring that the intended sorts are disjoint.
findings.controlling_evidence: The first-order coding uses unary predicates to distinguish these sorts and relativizes to each original domain; tagged isomorphic copies preserve the hypotheses and make those unions well defined without accidental overlap.
findings.required_translation_handling: Arrange disjoint tagged isomorphic copies of the element and sequence sorts, and of the two sides, before taking the unions; add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-021 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 24-36, construction of D_M and D

findings.finding: The proof literally conjoins all true bounded-rank sentences and disjoins over all E-models, then calls both operations finite only 'up to logical equivalence'.
findings.controlling_evidence: The cited finiteness proposition supplies finitely many equivalence classes, so the legitimate finite formulas are obtained by choosing representatives of the relevant classes and distinct n-types.
findings.required_translation_handling: Choose one representative from each relevant equivalence class for both finite Boolean constructions and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-020 disclosure.

findings.finding: After binding and removing constant c, the resulting sentence F is placed in L(L) even though its model class and the next line correctly use L-prime=L minus {c}.
findings.controlling_evidence: The quantifier operation eliminates the fresh constant, so F belongs to the reduced language L-prime; the displayed Mod subscript already confirms this.
findings.required_translation_handling: Place F in L(L-prime) and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-019 disclosure.

findings.finding: The source says 'Similarly for atomic formulas' even though its abstract logic contains only sentences and has defined no satisfaction relation for formulas with free variables.
findings.controlling_evidence: The later induction embedding first-order logic requires ordinary atomic sentences, formed with constants, to be present with their usual semantics; Boolean closure then handles sentence connectives.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the atomic-sentence base clause explicitly and keep Boolean closure for the other connectives, with an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-018 disclosure.

findings.finding: M-star interprets new symbols P,Q, but the analogous N-star is assigned P-prime,Q-prime even though both must be structures for one shared language inside the ambient model.
findings.controlling_evidence: The relativization and first-order coding sentences compare the two sides in one vocabulary; the same P,Q symbols must encode S,T on M-star and S-prime,T-prime on N-star.
findings.required_translation_handling: Let N-star interpret the same symbols P,Q by S-prime,T-prime and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-017 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 17-21, ordinary first-order logic as an abstract logic

findings.finding: The source says first-order sentences are built from the constants in L, omitting the predicate symbols that its relational languages explicitly permit.
findings.controlling_evidence: The preceding introduction defines the chapter's languages as containing predicate symbols and individual constants, and atomic first-order formulas require the predicate vocabulary.
findings.required_translation_handling: Say that the sentences are built using the symbols of L and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-016 disclosure.

findings.finding: The renamed structure M-prime is said to correspond to the language L rather than to the original structure M.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed biconditional compares M,E with their renamed counterparts M-prime,E-prime; a structure cannot be the renamed counterpart of a language.
findings.required_translation_handling: Say that M-prime is the L-prime structure corresponding to M and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The domain of N invokes the interpretation of fresh R in the unexpanded L-structure M, where R has no interpretation.
findings.controlling_evidence: The same clause supplies X as R's interpretation in the expansion of M, so the intended fibre is defined by X(a,b_1,...,b_n).
findings.required_translation_handling: Define the domain by X(a,b_1,...,b_n) and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-002 disclosure.

findings.finding: The property quantifies over arbitrary X and parameters while calling the resulting fibre a substructure, although the chapter permits constants and OpenLogic structures have nonempty domains.
findings.controlling_evidence: For a relational language with constants, a subset supports the indicated substructure only when it is nonempty and contains every original constant interpretation.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the nonempty-and-contains-constants admissibility condition for the fibre and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-003 disclosure.

findings.finding: The property gives E a finite semantic support but omits that E belongs to the logic over that finite sublanguage, a fact used twice in the following proofs.
findings.controlling_evidence: Both the partial-isomorphism proof and the Lindström proof invoke this property to work with E in L(L-prime) for finite L-prime; first-order logic has the intended stronger property because every sentence has a finite vocabulary.
findings.required_translation_handling: Require E to belong to L(L-prime) as well as have satisfaction determined by the L-prime reduct, and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-004 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 74-80, definition of the coding relation I

findings.finding: The source calls two finite sequences 'isomorphic' and individually satisfying a back-and-forth condition, neither of which is the earlier definition of membership in a family of partial isomorphisms.
findings.controlling_evidence: The chosen family mathcal I already witnesses partial isomorphism; I(a,b) should hold exactly when the coordinate map a_i to b_i belongs to that family.
findings.required_translation_handling: Code membership of the coordinate map in mathcal I and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-005 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 80-118 and figure, ambient coding structure

findings.finding: The ambient coding structure reuses M, thereby making the original M and M-star appear to be substructures of themselves, and the second starred-domain notation is malformed as Domain{N}*.
findings.controlling_evidence: The proof needs three distinct structures: the original M, its extension M-star, and an ambient structure containing the M and N sides. Its Löwenheim-Skolem model must likewise remain distinct from the internal M_0 and N_0.
findings.required_translation_handling: Name the ambient structure K and its enumerable model K_0, use Domain{M^*} and Domain{N^*}, update the figure/caption, and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-006 disclosure.

findings.finding: D_1 is called first-order even though it asserts the truth and falsity of an arbitrary abstract L-sentence by relativization.
findings.controlling_evidence: Relativization and Boolean closure yield an L-sentence D_1; only the structural coding assertion D_2 is first-order and is available in a normal logic.
findings.required_translation_handling: Classify D_1 as an L-sentence and D_2 as first-order, then add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-007 disclosure.

findings.finding: The lemma treats its constructed first-order sentence D as an L-sentence with ordinary first-order semantics, but does not assume the normality that supplies that embedding.
findings.controlling_evidence: The preceding chapter remark establishes F less-than-or-equal-to L for normal logics and explicitly permits first-order sentences to be taken as members of every normal logic.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add normality to the lemma hypothesis and an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-008 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proof reuses E for the first-order sentences conjoined into D_M, shadowing the fixed abstract sentence E.
findings.controlling_evidence: The chapter explicitly reserves A,B,... for first-order formulas and E,F,... for abstract sentences; using A here keeps the two roles distinct.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use A as the bound first-order-sentence variable and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-009 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 38-44, converse direction of the lemma

findings.finding: Both occurrences of D indexed by structure N omit braces, leaving Struct{N} outside the intended subscript.
findings.controlling_evidence: D_M was defined with the entire structure symbol as its subscript, and these occurrences instantiate that same definition at N.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use D_{Struct{N}} twice and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-010 disclosure.

findings.finding: The characterization assumes only Compactness and Löwenheim-Skolem, although the proof uses all the normal-logic closure properties and the parenthetical equivalence uses F less-than-or-equal-to L.
findings.controlling_evidence: The entire preceding section defines normality, proves F less-than-or-equal-to every normal logic, and the later proof invokes Expansion, Isomorphism, Relativization, Boolean, and Quantifier Properties.
findings.required_translation_handling: State that L is normal and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-011 disclosure.

findings.finding: The source forms unique minimal unions without arranging compatible overlaps, takes a subsequence without explaining why the reindexed pairs still satisfy I_n, and later combines element, sequence, and natural-number sorts without disjoint preparation.
findings.controlling_evidence: Isomorphic copies can share precisely the common constant interpretations and otherwise have disjoint domains; agreement on atomic sentences makes the overlap compatible. A subsequence m_n with m_n at least n retains I_n because higher back-and-forth rank implies lower rank. Tagged copies keep the coding sorts distinct.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the compatible-copy, rank-preserving reindexing, and tagged-sort preparation before taking the unions, then add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-012 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 82-109, ambient coding structure and compactness model

findings.finding: The ambient coding structure is named M even though M and M-star already denote the union on one side, and the compactness model M-star then collides with that earlier M-star.
findings.controlling_evidence: The proof needs the side structures M,M-star,N,N-star, a distinct ambient K, and a distinct compactness model K-star.
findings.required_translation_handling: Rename the ambient structure K and its compactness model K-star throughout and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-013 disclosure.

findings.finding: The coding sentence asserts M_n models E and N_n does not model E with ordinary first-order satisfaction, although E is an arbitrary abstract L-sentence.
findings.controlling_evidence: Every other truth assertion about E in the chapter uses models_L, and Relativization is exactly what makes those abstract-satisfaction clauses expressible.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use models_L in both clauses and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-014 disclosure.

findings.finding: Compactness is applied to the single sentence D and claimed to yield a nonstandard order element, but D itself has the original standard ordered model and does not force any element above every standard numeral.
findings.controlling_evidence: Adding a fresh constant d and the type {bar n < d : n in Nat} yields a finitely satisfiable set: each finite fragment is realized by a sufficiently large standard number. Compactness then gives d a genuinely nonstandard value.
findings.required_translation_handling: Apply Compactness to D together with the fresh-constant type, identify n-star with d's value, and add an adjacent OLTEMODLIN-015 disclosure.
